content:
Reconstruct the visible indoor scene from one RGB photograph using SceneAct and Blender.
Infer geometry and a camera matching the reference viewpoint, perspective and framing.
Use separate 3D meshes for architecture, furniture and visible objects, preserving colors,
proportions, placement, occlusions and materials. Do not use the reference as a texture,
background or projected image. No ground-truth calibration or other views are available.

Return a complete, runnable Python program inside one ```python code block. Each execution
starts in a fresh Blender process. Programs can use numpy, sceneact and bpy. Use SceneAct
for geometry and relationships; bpy may customize lighting, materials and camera settings.
Do not render or save files in the program: the fixed runner saves and renders once after
execution, using your active camera. Do not access external files, network or other models.
When satisfied after inspecting a rendering, reply exactly DONE. The last successful build
is submitted automatically. Budget includes all planning, corrections and review calls.

Coverage and verification procedure:
Before building, record a short reference inventory in program comments: major visible
objects, their approximate normalized image bounds, distinctive visible parts, overlaps,
and uncertain or occluded regions. These are estimates from this input, not calibration.
Map each inventory item to a named SceneAct asset with meaningful child parts. A valid
hierarchy verifies only the parts you emitted; it does not establish image completeness.
Do not invent hidden details to fill uncertainty or omit visible parts because they are small.
For composite objects, match the overall silhouette and the distribution of occupied space
and gaps before adding fine repeated details. Estimate component sizes relative to their
parent and nearby objects from the reference. A correct outer bounding box alone does not
ensure the correct internal density, component proportions or visible coverage. Keep these
parameters explicit so that a later revision can change them without rebuilding the design.

Use the first execution for a complete scene, leaving the second available for correction.
After a successful render, compare the reference inventory against the full rendered view:
missing or extra visible parts, silhouette, internal gaps, relative sizes, overlaps and image
bounds. Identify the largest supported discrepancies before revising. If many objects share
a displacement or scale error, consider camera/framing; if a discrepancy is local, consider
that object's parameters. Neither pattern proves a unique cause. Preserve matching objects
and their editable hierarchy while correcting the supported discrepancies. Do not impose
one fixed density, camera, object count or parameter adjustment across different inputs.
An isolated-object view, if supplied, can clarify membership and silhouette, but its full-image
score is not evidence that removing the rest of the scene improves the reconstruction.
Keep unresolved mappings and occluded geometry explicitly uncertain.

Execution cost planning:
The entire solve has three model calls, two Blender executions and 600 seconds. A short
Python loop can generate thousands of Blender objects before any image exists. Plan a
compact complete first build so that realization and the runner's render can finish with
time for review. Do not change the runner's resource policy or rendering settings to evade
this budget. Use geometry complexity as the controllable cost.
Before returning code, estimate expanded primitive counts in comments, including nested
loops and helper calls. In this implementation, each ball, rod and box emits a separate
mesh and marker; a fillet_box can expand to 26 primitives; sweep_tube with n points emits
2*n-1 primitives. Cloning and layout helpers duplicate their contents. Boolean operands
also incur mesh creation and modifier work. Count these expansions, not just named assets.
Aim initially for a few hundred primitive meshes across the whole scene, as a planning
heuristic rather than a measured runtime guarantee or fixed object count. Allocate detail
according to visible pixel size, silhouette and gaps. If the estimate reaches thousands,
simplify repeated microstructure before execution while retaining every inventory object
and its meaningful editable parts. Represent unresolved surface detail with shared materials
and restrained procedural shading; retain geometric detail that changes visible contours,
openings or occlusions. Avoid nested per-element decoration below the image resolution.
Use short, adaptively spaced tube paths for visible curves, concentrating points at bends.
Avoid many nearly identical Boolean slices to approximate one hollow shape; use a small
number of appropriate SceneAct solids and cutters, preserving the visible opening. Prefer
boxes or scaled balls where their silhouettes suffice; reserve fillet_box for parts whose
rounded edges matter. Keep a small reusable material palette for each surface family rather
than generating a distinct random color and material for every tiny primitive. Keep parent
assets, semantic child parts, and support relations intact during simplification.
If execution times out without an image, report that completion failed and the bottleneck
is unknown unless logs locate it. When a retry remains, reduce expanded primitive counts,
Boolean operations and material proliferation in the complete program. Do not infer camera,
coverage or appearance defects from a timeout. A reduced-cost build still needs execution
and rendered-image verification; simplification alone is not evidence of success.

Execution verification:
realize(scene) clears Blender to an empty factory scene. Configure the world, camera,
lighting and materials after realization; do not assume a default world exists. When setting
world nodes, use this initialization after realize:
    sc = bpy.context.scene
    if sc.world is None:
        sc.world = bpy.data.worlds.new('SceneWorld')
    sc.world.use_nodes = True
    background = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.get('Background')
    if background is None:
        background = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.new('ShaderNodeBackground')
    output = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.get('World Output')
    if output is None:
        output = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputWorld')
    sc.world.node_tree.links.new(background.outputs['Background'], output.inputs['Surface'])
Before returning code, check API arguments, positive dimensions, noncoincident rod endpoints,
and fillet radii against the smallest dimension. If execution fails, use the actual traceback
to repair the program. A failed execution without an image supplies no rendered visual
feedback: do not treat it as evidence for unrelated camera or geometry changes. Preserve
explicit failures and unknowns; do not claim verification when no successful render exists.

SceneAct API (all coordinates in a world frame with Z up; angles in degrees):
from sceneact import *
Scene(name='Scene'), Asset(name='Asset'), Part(name, *nodes)
parent.include(name, node) attaches an asset/part while preserving its world position.
parent.members[name] retrieves a child; parent.remove(name) detaches it.
node.clone() returns an independent subtree. scene.replicate(name, new_name) duplicates an asset.
box(size=(x,y,z), center=(x,y,z), color=(r,g,b), opacity=1)
ball(radius, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
rod(radius, start=(x,y,z), end=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
rod(radius, length=h, center=(0,0,0), axis='+z', color=(1,1,1))
fillet_box(size=(x,y,z), radius=r, center=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
sweep_tube(points=[(x,y,z), ...], radius=.03, color=(1,1,1))
assemble(nodes, name='Assembly') groups shapes without merging their meshes.
fuse(*nodes), subtract(base,*cutters), overlap(*nodes), exclusive(left,right) construct solids.
node.move(offset), node.turn(axis, degrees, pivot=None), node.resize(factors, pivot=None)
modify a node and its descendants. node.turn(euler=(rx,ry,rz)) applies X, then Y, then Z.
Default rotation/scale pivot is the geometry's world-space bounding-box center.
shifted(node, offset), turned(node, axis, degrees, pivot=None, euler=None),
resized(node, factors, pivot=None) perform the same operations on independent copies.
node.paint(color, opacity=1) applies color to the subtree; node.rgba reads its finish.
node.centroid, node.dimensions, node.limits give AABB center, size, (minimum,maximum).
node.landmark('top'), node.landmark('front_left_bottom') return bounding-box anchors.
node.extreme(direction) returns a support point; projected_span(node,direction) returns bounds
along a unit direction; projected_width(node,direction) returns their difference.
snap(node, target, source_anchor='bottom', target_anchor='top', offset=(0,0,0)) returns a copy.
A target can also be a world point; then omit target_anchor.
abut(node, target, axis='+z', gap=0) places a copy after a target boundary.
center_on(node, target, axes=('x','y','z')) aligns selected center coordinates.
offset_at(node, reference, offsets) positions selected coordinates; None preserves a coordinate.
repeat_line(nodes, axis='+x', spacing=1) uses equal center spacing, keeping the first fixed.
pile(nodes, axis='+z', gap=0) spaces bounding surfaces, keeping the first fixed.
lattice(nodes, rows=None, columns=None, spacing=(1,1), plane='xy', center=(0,0,0), order='row-major')
orbit(nodes, radius, axis='+z', center=(0,0,0), start=0, sweep=360, orient=False, rotation_offset=0)
Layout functions return assemblies of independent copies.
scene.bind(source,target,source_anchor='bottom',target_anchor='top',offset=(0,0,0))
registers a persistent relation between scene members; scene.settle() updates dependencies.
realize(scene) settles constraints and creates Blender geometry, clearing Blender first.
set_view(position,target,lens=35,sensor=36,shift=(0,0)) creates the active camera.
area_emitter(position,power=500,size=5,target=(0,0,0),color=(1,1,1)) creates an area light.
Call realize before setting the camera and lighting. Estimate the input viewpoint yourself.

Example:
from sceneact import *
scene = Scene()
table = Asset('table')
table.include('top', box((1.4,.8,.08), center=(0,0,.75), color=(.4,.2,.1)))
for x in (-.6,.6):
    for y in (-.3,.3):
        table.include(f'leg_{x}_{y}', box((.07,.07,.7), center=(x,y,.35)))
scene.include('table', table)
scene.include('floor', box((6,6,.1), center=(0,0,-.05), color=(.6,.6,.6)))
realize(scene)
set_view((3,-4,2), (0,0,.7), lens=40)
area_emitter((0,-2,4), power=1000)

```python
# Reference inventory and visual anchors (estimates, normalized x/y):
# The input is a vertical slide containing two separate photographs, not one
# calibrated room view. The lower photo occupies approximately (0.03,0.65)
# to (0.94,1.00): a long foreground control desk overlaps the wall cabinets,
# with a smaller console at the far right. The cabinet tops and desk edges
# recede to the right; the floor is visible in the foreground and right aisle.
# The separate upper photo (0.03,0.19)-(0.52,0.64) shows a yellow GRID
# demonstration panel with black wiring, red round lamps, amber square lamps,
# switches and small labels. Its exact location in the photographed room is
# uncertain; here it is mounted on the right wall as a readable exhibit.
# The lower photo's wall/floor junction and rear room corners are partly hidden.
#
# Anchor estimates below describe a landscape reconstruction of the lower
# photograph, rather than the collage's page coordinates. They provide an
# operational framing diagnostic, not measured camera calibration.
# Estimated expanded primitive count: room and furnishings ~35, cabinet meters
# ~90, main console controls ~90, GRID panel and wiring ~60, lighting ~8:
# approximately 280-320 meshes, depending on control distribution.

from sceneact import *
import bpy
import math
import json
from mathutils import Vector

# Major scene and camera parameters are intentionally separate.
ROOM_W = 9.0
ROOM_D = 6.8
ROOM_H = 3.4
CAMERA_POSITION = (8.7, -12.8, 7.3)
CAMERA_TARGET = (0.0, 0.25, 1.25)
CAMERA_LENS = 39
IMAGE_WIDTH, IMAGE_HEIGHT = 1920, 1080

scene = Scene("1970s grid dispatch control room")
ivory = (0.68, 0.65, 0.59)
wall = (0.76, 0.74, 0.69)
floor_color = (0.35, 0.32, 0.29)
cabinet = (0.68, 0.67, 0.63)
face = (0.82, 0.81, 0.75)
dark = (0.12, 0.12, 0.11)
black = (0.035, 0.035, 0.03)
yellow = (0.95, 0.70, 0.12)
red = (0.72, 0.035, 0.025)
amber = (0.98, 0.47, 0.025)

def add_box(parent, name, size, center, color):
    parent.include(name, box(size=size, center=center, color=color))

def add_rod(parent, name, radius, start, end, color):
    parent.include(name, rod(radius=radius, start=start, end=end, color=color))

# Architecture. Camera faces the back wall; the right return frames the room.
architecture = Asset("Architecture")
add_box(architecture, "floor", (ROOM_W, ROOM_D, .12),
        (0, 0, -.06), floor_color)
add_box(architecture, "back_wall", (ROOM_W, .12, ROOM_H),
        (0, ROOM_D/2, ROOM_H/2), wall)
add_box(architecture, "right_wall", (.12, ROOM_D, ROOM_H),
        (ROOM_W/2, 0, ROOM_H/2), wall)
add_box(architecture, "ceiling", (ROOM_W, ROOM_D, .08),
        (0, 0, ROOM_H + .04), wall)
add_box(architecture, "back_skirt", (ROOM_W, .06, .12),
        (0, ROOM_D/2-.09, .06), (0.42, .40, .37))
scene.include("architecture", architecture)

# Long cabinet bank with a regular array of square framed indicators.
bank = Asset("Main_wall_instrument_bank")
add_box(bank, "cabinet_body", (6.75, .38, 2.45),
        (-1.05, 3.13, 1.35), cabinet)
add_box(bank, "top_fascia", (6.75, .05, .30),
        (-1.05, 2.91, 2.42), face)
# Nine rows/columns are intentionally estimated rather than calibrated.
for col in range(10):
    x = -4.03 + col * .43
    for row in range(4):
        z = .57 + row * .43
        add_box(bank, f"meter_frame_{col}_{row}", (.31, .045, .31),
                (x, 2.905, z), dark)
        add_box(bank, f"meter_face_{col}_{row}", (.255, .025, .255),
                (x, 2.874, z), face)
        # Single pointer gives the small panels an unmistakable instrument face.
        add_rod(bank, f"pointer_{col}_{row}", .008,
                (x-.055, 2.852, z-.045),
                (x+.035, 2.852, z+.055), dark)
# Wide ventilation grille in the middle-right part of the wall bank.
add_box(bank, "vent_recess", (1.22, .05, .80),
        (1.08, 2.90, 1.40), dark)
for i in range(7):
    add_box(bank, f"vent_slat_{i}", (1.12, .035, .035),
            (1.08, 2.86, 1.09 + i*.10), face)
for i in range(5):
    x = 2.05 + i*.30
    for j in range(4):
        z = .74 + j*.37
        add_box(bank, f"right_frame_{i}_{j}", (.22,.04,.25),
                (x,2.90,z), dark)
        add_box(bank, f"right_face_{i}_{j}", (.17,.025,.20),
                (x,2.87,z), face)
scene.include("wall_instruments", bank)

# Main desk: long horizontal writing ledge and a rising instrument surface.
desk = Asset("Long_sloping_operator_console")
DESK_X = -1.05
DESK_Y = -.25
DESK_LEN = 6.35
add_box(desk, "pedestal", (DESK_LEN, 1.15, .68),
        (DESK_X, DESK_Y+.15, .36), (0.36, .34, .31))
add_box(desk, "writing_ledge", (DESK_LEN+.12, .68, .10),
        (DESK_X, DESK_Y-.56, .78), face)

# Sloping surface runs from y=-0.48,z=.83 up to y=.60,z=1.34.
slope_angle = math.degrees(math.atan2(.51, 1.08))
slope = box((DESK_LEN, 1.195, .10),
            center=(DESK_X, DESK_Y+.06, 1.085), color=face)
slope.turn(axis="x", degrees=slope_angle)
desk.include("sloped_control_surface", slope)
add_box(desk, "rear_lip", (DESK_LEN, .07, .10),
        (DESK_X, DESK_Y+.60, 1.36), cabinet)

# Surface coordinate helper and controls protruding along the surface normal.
def desk_surface(x, t):
    return (x, DESK_Y-.48 + 1.08*t, .84 + .51*t)

normal = (0, -math.sin(math.radians(slope_angle)),
          math.cos(math.radians(slope_angle)))
for i in range(15):
    x = DESK_X - 2.91 + i*.415
    # Dark small switch blocks form the dense operational pattern.
    for j, t in enumerate((.20, .43, .67, .86)):
        p = desk_surface(x, t)
        r = .028 if j != 2 else .041
        add_rod(desk, f"control_{i}_{j}", r, p,
                (p[0]+normal[0]*.045, p[1]+normal[1]*.045,
                 p[2]+normal[2]*.045),
                dark if (i+j)%5 else red)
    if i % 3 == 0:
        p = desk_surface(x+.13, .71)
        add_rod(desk, f"large_dial_{i}", .067, p,
                (p[0],p[1]+normal[1]*.025,p[2]+normal[2]*.025), dark)
scene.include("main_console", desk)

# Small free-standing console at the far right, with its own sloped panel.
small = Asset("Right_independent_console")
add_box(small, "base", (1.40,.82,.78), (3.34,2.18,.39), cabinet)
panel = box((1.42,.87,.08), center=(3.34,2.18,.87), color=face)
panel.turn(axis="x", degrees=15)
small.include("control_top", panel)
for i in range(6):
    for j in range(3):
        x = 2.81+i*.21
        y = 1.88+j*.23
        z = .87 + (y-2.18)*math.tan(math.radians(15)) + .045
        add_rod(small, f"switch_{i}_{j}", .025, (x,y,z),
                (x,y-.01,z+.045), dark if (i+j)%4 else red)
scene.include("independent_console", small)

# Yellow GRID mimic panel on the right return. Geometry lies in the YZ plane.
grid = Asset("Yellow_GRID_mimic_panel")
GRID_X = 4.42
GRID_Y = 1.02
GRID_Z = 1.93
GRID_W = 1.65
GRID_H = 1.65
add_box(grid, "yellow_backboard", (.08,GRID_W,GRID_H),
        (GRID_X,GRID_Y,GRID_Z), yellow)

def grid_wire(name, yz_points, radius=.018, color=black):
    for k in range(len(yz_points)-1):
        a, b = yz_points[k], yz_points[k+1]
        add_rod(grid, f"{name}_{k}", radius,
                (GRID_X-.055, GRID_Y+a[0], GRID_Z+a[1]),
                (GRID_X-.055, GRID_Y+b[0], GRID_Z+b[1]), color)

# Vertical bus with rectangular branches mirrors the diagram's recognizable form.
grid_wire("vertical_bus", [(0,-.72),(0,.70)])
grid_wire("upper_loop", [(0,.43),(-.29,.43),(-.29,.12),(.28,.12),
                         (.28,.43),(0,.43)])
grid_wire("middle_loop", [(0,.04),(-.29,.04),(-.29,-.25),(.28,-.25),
                          (.28,.04),(0,.04)])
grid_wire("lower_branch", [(0,-.38),(-.35,-.38),(-.35,-.53)])
grid_wire("right_branch", [(0,-.38),(.36,-.38),(.36,-.53)])
for k,(dy,dz) in enumerate([(-.22,.27),(-.07,.27),(.09,.27),(.23,.27),
                             (-.22,-.11),(-.07,-.11),(.09,-.11),(.23,-.11),
                             (-.35,-.53),(.36,-.53)]):
    add_box(grid, f"amber_frame_{k}", (.035,.125,.125),
            (GRID_X-.075,GRID_Y+dy,GRID_Z+dz), black)
    add_box(grid, f"amber_lamp_{k}", (.025,.085,.085),
            (GRID_X-.10,GRID_Y+dy,GRID_Z+dz), amber)
for k,(dy,dz) in enumerate([(0,.58),(0,-.65),(-.58,.48),(-.58,.23),
                             (-.58,-.02),(-.58,-.27),(.57,.43)]):
    add_rod(grid, f"red_indicator_{k}", .055,
            (GRID_X-.06,GRID_Y+dy,GRID_Z+dz),
            (GRID_X-.115,GRID_Y+dy,GRID_Z+dz), red)
for k,dz in enumerate((.37,.02,-.34,-.57)):
    add_rod(grid, f"selector_{k}", .055,
            (GRID_X-.06,GRID_Y-.67,GRID_Z+dz),
            (GRID_X-.14,GRID_Y-.67,GRID_Z+dz), black)
scene.include("grid_mimic", grid)

# Simple visible ceiling fixtures. Their geometry is retained as editable parts.
fixtures = Asset("Ceiling_fluorescent_troffers")
for i, x in enumerate((-2.6, 0, 2.6)):
    add_box(fixtures, f"housing_{i}", (1.65,.48,.055),
            (x,0,ROOM_H-.04), cabinet)
    add_box(fixtures, f"diffuser_{i}", (1.50,.36,.025),
            (x,0,ROOM_H-.075), (0.95,.94,.87))
scene.include("ceiling_lights", fixtures)

realize(scene)

# World is created explicitly because realize clears Blender's default scene.
sc = bpy.context.scene
if sc.world is None:
    sc.world = bpy.data.worlds.new("SceneWorld")
sc.world.use_nodes = True
background = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.get("Background")
if background is None:
    background = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.new("ShaderNodeBackground")
output = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.get("World Output")
if output is None:
    output = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.new("ShaderNodeOutputWorld")
sc.world.node_tree.links.new(background.outputs["Background"],
                             output.inputs["Surface"])
background.inputs["Color"].default_value = (0.68, .66, .62, 1)
background.inputs["Strength"].default_value = .45

set_view(CAMERA_POSITION, CAMERA_TARGET, lens=CAMERA_LENS, sensor=36)
panorama_camera = sc.camera
panorama_camera.name = "Camera_Panorama"

# A second editable camera aims at the console and yellow panel. The active
# camera remains the panorama for the fixed runner.
bpy.ops.object.camera_add(location=(7.8, -5.3, 3.4))
detail_camera = bpy.context.object
detail_camera.name = "Camera_Console_GRID_Closeup"
detail_target = Vector((2.3, 1.0, 1.35))
detail_camera.rotation_euler = (detail_target-detail_camera.location).to_track_quat("-Z","Y").to_euler()
detail_camera.data.lens = 48
sc.camera = panorama_camera

area_emitter((0,-1.0,3.15), power=1000, size=5.0, target=(0,1,0))
area_emitter((-3,-2.5,3.0), power=550, size=3.0, target=(-1,1,1))
area_emitter((3,1.0,3.0), power=400, size=2.5, target=(2,1,1))

# Small editable German labels on the yellow panel. Text is positioned just in
# front of the panel, facing into the room along negative X.
def grid_label(name, text, y, z, size=.065):
    curve = bpy.data.curves.new(name, type="FONT")
    curve.body = text
    curve.size = size
    curve.extrude = .0005
    obj = bpy.data.objects.new(name, curve)
    sc.collection.objects.link(obj)
    obj.location = (GRID_X-.125, GRID_Y+y, GRID_Z+z)
    # Local text X points toward negative Y; text Y points upward.
    obj.rotation_euler = (math.pi/2, 0, -math.pi/2)
    return obj

grid_label("label_grid", "GRID", -.20, .69, .09)
grid_label("label_fault", "FEHLER-STELLE K", .10, .55, .045)
grid_label("label_switch", "SCHALTER", -.73, -.70, .042)

# Use emissive indicator materials on named lamp meshes while retaining their
# original semantic objects. Material matching is intentionally conservative.
def emission_material(name, color, strength):
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    mat.diffuse_color = (*color, 1)
    mat.use_nodes = True
    bsdf = mat.node_tree.nodes.get("Principled BSDF")
    if bsdf:
        if "Emission Color" in bsdf.inputs:
            bsdf.inputs["Emission Color"].default_value = (*color, 1)
            bsdf.inputs["Emission Strength"].default_value = strength
        elif "Emission" in bsdf.inputs:
            bsdf.inputs["Emission"].default_value = (*color, 1)
    return mat

lamp_red = emission_material("Indicator red illuminated", (.65,.025,.01), 1.3)
lamp_amber = emission_material("Indicator amber illuminated", (1,.35,.015), 1.3)
troffer_mat = emission_material("Fluorescent diffuser", (.95,.91,.78), 1.1)
for obj in bpy.data.objects:
    n = obj.name.lower()
    if obj.type == "MESH":
        mat = None
        if "red_indicator" in n:
            mat = lamp_red
        elif "amber_lamp" in n:
            mat = lamp_amber
        elif "diffuser" in n:
            mat = troffer_mat
        if mat is not None:
            obj.data.materials.clear()
            obj.data.materials.append(mat)

# Organize the Blender objects into named collections based on their semantic
# SceneAct ancestry/name where available.
for cname in ("Architecture", "Wall instruments", "Main console",
              "Independent console", "GRID mimic panel", "Ceiling lights",
              "Cameras and lights"):
    if bpy.data.collections.get(cname) is None:
        col = bpy.data.collections.new(cname)
        sc.collection.children.link(col)

# SceneAct's asset hierarchy is preserved; camera and light objects are grouped.
equipment_col = bpy.data.collections["Cameras and lights"]
for obj in list(sc.objects):
    if obj.type in {"CAMERA", "LIGHT"}:
        for col in list(obj.users_collection):
            col.objects.unlink(obj)
        equipment_col.objects.link(obj)

sc.render.engine = "CYCLES"
sc.cycles.use_denoising = True
sc.render.image_settings.file_format = "PNG"
try:
    sc.view_settings.view_transform = "Filmic"
except Exception:
    pass

# Camera diagnostics: project actual identifiable geometry points at the
# requested aspect. Reference positions are estimates in the landscape crop.
anchors = [
    ("back_wall_left_top", (-4.5,3.34,3.4), (.06,.12)),
    ("back_wall_right_top", (4.5,3.34,3.4), (.86,.12)),
    ("bank_left_lower", (-4.425,2.90,.125), (.04,.62)),
    ("bank_right_upper", (2.325,2.90,2.575), (.70,.25)),
    ("desk_front_left", (-4.285,-1.15,.83), (.05,.91)),
    ("desk_front_right", (2.185,-1.15,.83), (.72,.88)),
    ("grid_upper_corner", (4.37,1.845,2.755), (.83,.27)),
    ("small_console_front", (4.04,1.77,.78), (.89,.65)),
]
```
